extracted.intended_audience: corporate communicators, investor relations officers, financial analysts, and accounting researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and evaluating the tone and content of earnings press releases vis-à-vis the firm's SEC-filed MD&A, with attention to credibility, litigation risk, and pickup-worthiness by financial media and analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimism–pessimism gap discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated analysts and algorithms compute the gap between press-release tone and MD&A tone for the same quarter; a gap larger than industry norm flags strategic obfuscation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the press-release vs MD&A optimism–pessimism gap within the industry-typical band. Large positive gaps (more optimistic in the release than MD&A) reduce credibility, invite analyst skepticism, and lower pickup-worthiness at top financial outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material-information consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Material adverse facts disclosed in the MD&A must also appear in the press release; selective omission triggers SEC and class-action attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure material adverse items appearing in the MD&A are not excluded from the press release. Selective omission is an anti-pattern that increases securities-law exposure and harms credibility with analysts and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-vs-backward language balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings releases that lean heavily on forward-looking optimism while burying backward-looking pessimism are flagged by analysts; balance the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overemphasizing forward-looking upbeat language while minimizing discussion of recent negative outcomes. Balanced treatment of past performance and forward guidance reduces the appearance of spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetric framing of beats and misses
rubrics_metrics.description: Both beats and misses should be presented in the same language register; treating misses with extra hedging (and beats with extra emphasis) is flagged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame positive and negative results consistently—use symmetric wording and similar levels of emphasis and hedging for beats and misses to avoid perceived selective framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-MD&A consistency check
rubrics_metrics.description: Before release, draft MD&A and press release together so the language differential is monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational practice: prepare and review the press release alongside the MD&A to monitor tone differentials and correct inconsistencies prior to filing/release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-comparable optimism band
rubrics_metrics.description: Across an industry, peer firms' optimism gaps cluster; releases far from the cluster on the optimism side invite skepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark your release's tone against industry peers. Staying within the peer cluster for optimism/pessimism helps maintain credibility and reduces the chance of negative analyst or media reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-emptive bad-news framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative news that will appear in MD&A is better introduced in the release than discovered by analysts in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively surface and contextualize anticipated negative disclosures in the press release so analysts and journalists do not 'discover' them in the MD&A, which can amplify negative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation-risk awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Davis & Tama-Sweet's data align with later SEC enforcement actions for misleading optimism in 8-K releases; aggressive optimism gaps create securities-law exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that aggressive optimism or selective disclosure differences between press releases and MD&A can attract SEC enforcement and class-action risk. Tone management is not just reputational but also legal-risk management.
